question: Which sage did Valmiki ask about a man of outstanding virtue?
Sanskrit_only_top1_sanskrit: भीष्म उवाच एवमेतन्महाप्राज्ञ यथा वदसि बुद्धिमन्। दुर्लभः पुरुषः कश्चिदेभिर्युक्तो गुणैः शुभैः॥
Sanskrit_only_top1_english: You are highly intelligent, O Yudhishthira! It is what you say. The person is very rare who is endued with all those good qualities.
English_only_top1_sanskrit: साधु पृच्छ नरश्रेष्ठ वाल्मीकिं मुनिपुङ्गवम्। शत्रुघ्नस्त्वब्रवीत्सर्वान्कौतूहलसमन्वितान्॥ सैनिकानक्षमोऽस्माकं परिप्रष्टुमिहेदृशः। आश्चर्याणि बहूनीह भवन्त्यस्याश्रमे मुनेः॥
English_only_top1_english: O foremost of men, do you ask particularly, about this, Vālmīki, the foremost of ascetics. They being all thus struck with curiosity, Satrughna said: It is not proper for us, O You soldiers, to question him in this way. There are many such wonders in the hermitage of this ascetic.
Sanskrit_English_top1_sanskrit: ॐ तपः स्वाध्यायनिरतं तपस्वी वाग्विदां वरम्। नारदं परिपप्रच्छ वाल्मीकिर्मुनिपुङ्गवम्॥
Sanskrit_English_top1_english: The ascetic Vālmīki asked Nārada, the best of sages and foremost of those conversant with words, ever engaged in austerities and Vedic studies.

question: After meeting the Nishada king Guha, where did Rama dismiss his charioteer?
expected_answer: On the banks of the Ganges at Srigaverapura
Sanskrit_only_top1_sanskrit: तत्र राजा गुहो नाम रामस्यात्मसमः सखा। निषादजात्यो बलवान् स्थपतिश्चेति विश्रुतः॥
Sanskrit_only_top1_english: There lived at the place a king named Guha, a friend to Răma, dear as his own self, a Nişāda by birth, powerful and famed as the lord of the Nişādas.
English_only_top1_sanskrit: शृङ्गवेरपुरे सुतं गङ्गाकूले व्यसर्जयत्। गुहमासाद्य धर्मात्मा निषादाधिपतिं प्रियम्॥ गुहेन सहितो रामो लक्ष्मणेन च सीतया।
English_only_top1_english: Rāma met with the virtuous and beloved king of the Nişādas; and then in company with Guha, Laksmana, and Sita, Rama dismissed his charioteer on the banks of the Ganges at Srigaverapura.
Sanskrit_English_top1_sanskrit: शृङ्गवेरपुरे सुतं गङ्गाकूले व्यसर्जयत्। गुहमासाद्य धर्मात्मा निषादाधिपतिं प्रियम्॥ गुहेन सहितो रामो लक्ष्मणेन च सीतया।
Sanskrit_English_top1_english: Rāma met with the virtuous and beloved king of the Nişādas; and then in company with Guha, Laksmana, and Sita, Rama dismissed his charioteer on the banks of the Ganges at Srigaverapura.

question: When Kaikeyi claimed the two boons she had been promised, what two things did she ask for?
expected_answer: The exile of Rama and the installation of Bharata
Sanskrit_only_top1_sanskrit: कथेयमभवत् तत्र त्वया या परिकीर्तिता। सुमनोधूपदीपानां सम्प्रदाने फलं प्रति॥ ततः पप्रच्छ दैत्येन्द्रः कवीन्द्रं प्रश्नमुत्तमम्॥
Sanskrit_only_top1_english: This very subject which you have introduced regarding the merits of the gift of flowers and incense and lamps, came up on the occasion. Indeed the king of the Daityas put this high question of Shukra that most learned of all ascetics.
English_only_top1_sanskrit: तस्याभिषेकसम्भारान्दृष्ट्वा भार्याऽथ कैकयी॥ पूर्वं दत्तवरा देवी वरमेनमयाचत। विवासं च रामस्य भरतस्याभिषेचनम्॥
English_only_top1_english: Beholding the provisions of the installation, that lady the king's consort, Kaikeyī, who had previously been promised two boons, even asked him for those viz., the exile of Ráma, and the installation of Bharata.
Sanskrit_English_top1_sanskrit: तस्याभिषेकसम्भारान्दृष्ट्वा भार्याऽथ कैकयी॥ पूर्वं दत्तवरा देवी वरमेनमयाचत। विवासं च रामस्य भरतस्याभिषेचनम्॥
Sanskrit_English_top1_english: Beholding the provisions of the installation, that lady the king's consort, Kaikeyī, who had previously been promised two boons, even asked him for those viz., the exile of Ráma, and the installation of Bharata.

question: Why did king Dasaratha banish his son Rama?
expected_answer: Because he was bound by duty to keep his promise
Sanskrit_only_top1_sanskrit: कामार्तश्च महाराजः पिता दशरथः स्वयम्॥ कैकेय्याः प्रियकामार्थं तं रामं नाभ्यषेचयत्।
Sanskrit_only_top1_english: Our father the king Daśaratha was entirely under the control of passions, and hence for the satisfaction of Kaikeyi did not install Rāma.-
English_only_top1_sanskrit: स सत्यवचनात् राजा धर्मपाशेन संयतः। विवासयामास सुतं रामं दशरथः प्रियम्॥
English_only_top1_english: Bound by the ties of duty in consequence of his promise, king Dasaratha banished his favourite son Rāma.
Sanskrit_English_top1_sanskrit: स सत्यवचनात् राजा धर्मपाशेन संयतः। विवासयामास सुतं रामं दशरथः प्रियम्॥
Sanskrit_English_top1_english: Bound by the ties of duty in consequence of his promise, king Dasaratha banished his favourite son Rāma.

question: After Dasaratha died, did Bharata accept the throne when Vasistha and the other Brahmanas pressed him to rule?
expected_answer: No. He refused the kingdom and went to the forest to seek Rama.
Sanskrit_only_top1_sanskrit: अर्हस्त्वमपि दातुं वै नादातुं भरतर्षभ। एवं ब्रुवाणं वीभत्सुं धर्मराजोऽप्यपूजयत्॥
Sanskrit_only_top1_english: You should give instead of refusing, O chief of Bharata's race!' Bibhatsu who was saying so was applauded by king Yudhishthira the just.
English_only_top1_sanskrit: गते तु तस्मिन् भरतो वसिष्ठप्रमुखैर्द्विजैः॥ नियुज्यमानो राज्याय नैच्छद् राज्यं महाबलः। स जगाम वनं वीरो रामपादप्रसादकः॥
English_only_top1_english: When king Dasaratha had passed away heaven, the mighty Bharata, although pressed by the Brāhmaṇas headed by Vasiştha, to rule the kingdom, did not wish for dominion. And that hero went the forest, with the view of propitiating Rāma.
Sanskrit_English_top1_sanskrit: गते तु तस्मिन् भरतो वसिष्ठप्रमुखैर्द्विजैः॥ नियुज्यमानो राज्याय नैच्छद् राज्यं महाबलः। स जगाम वनं वीरो रामपादप्रसादकः॥
Sanskrit_English_top1_english: When king Dasaratha had passed away heaven, the mighty Bharata, although pressed by the Brāhmaṇas headed by Vasiştha, to rule the kingdom, did not wish for dominion. And that hero went the forest, with the view of propitiating Rāma.

question: When the Ocean appeared and advised them, who built the causeway across the sea?
Sanskrit_only_top1_sanskrit: सृजन्तः शरवातान् किरन्तोऽर्जुनमाहवे। अभ्यवर्तन्त सहसा वार्योधा इव सागरम्॥
Sanskrit_only_top1_english: All these scattered and shot innumerable arrows at Arjuna in the battle, even as the masses of clouds suddenly pour forth showers of rain, that approach towards the vast ocean.
English_only_top1_sanskrit: दर्शयामास चात्मानं समुद्रः सरितां पतिः। समुद्रवचनाच्चैव नलं सेतुमकारयत्॥
English_only_top1_english: Then that lord of rivers, the Ocean, showed himself. And agreeably to the advice of the Ocean, Nala constructed a bridge (over the water.)

question: Who lured Rama far from the ashram by taking the form of a golden deer?
Sanskrit_only_top1_sanskrit: एवं रामाय कौरव्य वसिष्ठोऽकथयत् पुरा। तस्मात् सुवर्णदानाय प्रयतस्व नराधिप॥
Sanskrit_only_top1_english: Thus, O son of Kuru's race, did Vasishtha recite formerly this topic to Rama of Bhrigu's race. Do you, therefore, O king of men, try to make gifts of gold.
English_only_top1_sanskrit: तमब्रवीद् दशग्रीवो गच्छ सीतां प्रलोभय॥ रत्नशृङ्गो मृगो भूत्वा रत्नचित्रतनूरूहः। ध्रुवं सीता समालक्ष्य त्वां रामं चोदयिष्यति॥
English_only_top1_english: (There at) the ten-headed one replied to him "go and tempt Sita wearing the form of a deer with golden horns and a golden skin. It is certain that on beholding you she will send Rama after you".
Sanskrit_English_top1_sanskrit: तमब्रवीद् दशग्रीवो गच्छ सीतां प्रलोभय॥ रत्नशृङ्गो मृगो भूत्वा रत्नचित्रतनूरूहः। ध्रुवं सीता समालक्ष्य त्वां रामं चोदयिष्यति॥

question: How far did Hanuman say he leaped across the ocean to carry out Rama's work?
Sanskrit_only_top1_sanskrit: खानितः सगरेणायमप्रमेयो महोदधिः। कर्तुमर्हसि रामस्य ज्ञातेः कार्य महोदधिः॥
Sanskrit_only_top1_english: This measureless deep was dug out by (the king) Sagara.* And the great ocean shall surely help Rāma belonging to Sagara's race. *Sagara was a sovereign of Ayodhyā, belonging to the same family with Rāma.
English_only_top1_sanskrit: हनूमानुवाच कएष हनुमान् नाम सागरो येन लवित्तः। पृच्छामि त्वां नरश्रेष्ठ कथ्यतां यदि शक्यते॥
English_only_top1_english: Hanuman said: Who is he of the name of Hanuman who leaped over the ocean. O foremost of men I ask you, relate it if you can.

question: In Krishna's teaching to Arjuna, what does he say a person should be concerned with, and never with?
expected_answer: Concerned only with actions, never with their fruits
Sanskrit_only_top1_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच यदि प्रीतेन मे दत्तं संशये जीवितस्य वा। विद्याधनं श्रुतं वापि न तद् गन्धर्व रोचये॥
Sanskrit_only_top1_english: Arjuna said : O Gandharva, if you give me out of your satisfaction for obtaining life in a crisis, these horses and the wealth of science shall not accept it.
English_only_top1_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच अयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः। अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति॥
English_only_top1_english: Arjuna said What is the end of him, O Krishna who has not earned success in devotion, being not assiduous, and having a mind shaken off from devotion, through full of faith?
Sanskrit_English_top1_sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाच अयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः। अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति॥
